senses.gloss: to rest on; to rely, feel safe.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Samuel 1:6">Targ. II Sam. I, 6</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 88:8">Targ. Ps. LXXXVIII, 8</cite>.

<cite ref="Chagigah 20b:5">Ḥag. 20ᵇ</cite> <he>מִיסְמַךְ סָמְכָא דעתייהו</he> their mind is at rest (they feel safe that they cannot be seen).
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 71b:14">Ab. Zar. 71ᵇ</cite> <he>סמכא דעתיה</he> he feels sure (of his bargain); a. fr.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 3:2:2">Y. Sabb. III, 5ᵈ</cite> bot., v. <cite ref="A00407"><he>אֲדֵירָא</he></cite>.
Yeb. 119ᵃ סְמוֹךְ מיעוטא וכ׳ bring close, i.e. add. &c., v. מִיעוּטָא; Kidd. 80ᵃ; a. e.—Esp. to ordain (v. preced., a.
<cite ref="Onkelos Deuteronomy 34:9">Targ. Deut. XXXIV, 9</cite>).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 13b:12">Snh. 13ᵇ</cite> (expl. <he>סמיכת זקנים</he>, v. <cite ref="O01092"><he>סְמִיכוּת</he></cite>) <he>מִיסְמַךְ סבי</he> ordaining of elders.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 13b:12">Ib.</cite> <he>בירֹא ממש סַמְכִין ליה או בשמא סמכין ליה</he> Ms. M. must they ordain him by actually putting a hand on him, or merely by calling his name? <cite ref="Sanhedrin 13b:12">Ib.</cite> <he>וחד לא סָמֵיךְ</he> and one alone cannot ordain? <cite ref="Sanhedrin 14a:4">Ib. 14ᵃ</cite> <he>ור״מ … סַמְכֵיה</he> was it R. J. ben B. that ordained R. Meir? <cite ref="Sanhedrin 14a:10">Ib.</cite> <he>הוה מיטמר מלמיסמכיה</he> Ms. M. was on his guard not to be ordained.
Ib. סְמוֹכוּ לנא appoint for us as teachers, v. חֲמִיסִין; a. fr.—Part. pass. סָמִיךְ, סְמִיךְ
<cite ref="Pesachim 49a:16">Pes. 49ᵃ</cite> <he>תרי בני סְמִיכֵי</he> two sons both of whom were ordained teachers.—

senses.gloss: to press, stamp, make a thick mass.
units: <cite ref="Pesachim 116a:3">Pes. 116ᵃ</cite> <he>וצריך לסַמּוּכֵיה וכ׳</he> and you must make it a thick mass so as to be emblematical of clay (v. <cite ref="H01630"><he>חֲרוֹסֶת</he></cite>).

senses.gloss: to secure, esp. to refer to a depositary for payment; to draw an order for. Y. Kidd. III, 64ᵃ top סַמְּכֵיה גבי לוי he referred him to Levy (as his depositary).
units: <cite ref="Yoma 2a">Ib.</cite> <he>סַמְּכוּן … גבי זבונה</he> they secured the teacher by a deposit with a merchant. Y. Shebu. VII, 38ᵃ top, <cite ref="K01383"><he>כַּתָּפָא</he></cite>. Y. B. Mets. IV, beg. 9ᶜ; a. e.

senses.gloss: to give an order to. Ib. אנא בעי … דאַסְמִיכְתַּנִי I want to collect the money for which thou hast given me an order (at the banker’s).

to lean on; to find support; to give support. Y. Ber. II, 4ᶜ כל מילה … מַסְמְכִין לה מן וכ׳ whenever a proposition is not evident, they try to support it by a large number of Biblical passages; Pesik. R. s. 22 מַסְמְכִינָן, v. אֲתַר.
units: <cite ref="Moed Katan 5a:15">M. Kat. 5ᵃ</cite> <he>אַסְמְכָהּ אקרא</he> gave it support by reference to a Biblical verse.

<cite ref="Berakhot 19b:11">Ber. 19ᵇ</cite> <he>כל מילי … אַסְמְכִינְהוּ על וכ׳</he> they lean all rules of the Rabbis on the law, ‘Thou shalt not deviate’, v. <cite ref="O00408"><he>סוּר</he> I</cite>; a. e.

senses.gloss: to make substantial, put a thick layer on.
